rationale: Both use the same sound approach: sort the per-title counts, split them into layers of group sizes, swap each pair of a five-group and a three-group for two four-groups, then add up the prices. B's explicit groups literal and its explanatory comments are very readable, and taking the minimum for the conversion count is neat. However, B indexes counts[b-1] without checking, so it panics on any book ID outside 1-5. A guards against this. A's sentinel-and-difference loop is compact, and its comments explain it well. The package-level groupPrices table is also a reasonable choice. The two are close in clarity, and A's extra robustness tips it.
